subject: c12-chem
note: Marks are official (course structure, total 70). CBSE also says to cover all chapters even though no separate chapter-wise weightage is given. Chapters 11 to 14 are formative only and carry no theory marks. Question mix: remembering and understanding 28 marks (40%), applying 21 (30%), analysing, evaluating and creating 21 (30%). There is no overall choice, but 33% internal choice is given. Practical is 30 marks.
mistakes: Electrochemistry: check the sign and units. E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode, and use the correct n in the Nernst equation.
Chemical kinetics: the unit of the rate constant k depends on the order of the reaction.
Solutions: do not mix up molarity and molality, and note which one changes with temperature.
Coordination compounds: in names, write ligands in alphabetical order, then the metal with its oxidation state. Count ligands carefully for the formula and charge.
Organic conversions: write the reagent and conditions on every arrow. A missing reagent or condition can cost the step.
Draw structures neatly with the correct bonds, so the examiner can read each one.
order: Physical chemistry first: Chapters 1 to 3 (23 marks). Electrochemistry is the biggest single chapter at 9.
Then organic in order, Chapters 6 to 9 (26 marks), because the conversions link one chapter to the next.
Read the formative-only Chapters 11 to 14 last, for school assessment.
Do practical and record file work alongside the theory.
